answer: Each epoch the protocol issues every identity a randomized prompt — private seed, shuffled constraints — so a farm cannot rehearse one template. Replies are embedded and clustered: an honest agent's text carries an opal-like play of color, a fingerprint no one else shows, while N clones tuned to the same hidden structure sprout on one trellis wire and settle as a single cluster paid one share, not N. Escaping that harbor demands N genuinely divergent model stacks, maintained epoch after epoch, and every hull added makes the fleet's correlation easier to see. The farm's margin dies with scale.
